title: introduce commitment-telemetry-aggregator and latency-targeted autoscaler
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently make autoscaling decisions based on instantaneous utilization and simple thresholds which are noisy during traffic spikes. We need a proactive path that (1) aggregates tenant-level committed capacity signals into a stable time-windowed view, and (2) uses a latency-targeted predictive autoscaler to warm capacity before p99 latency SLOs are breached. This PR introduces two related components: a Commitment Telemetry Aggregator and a Latency-Targeted Autoscaler. Design: - Commitment Telemetry Aggregator: collects per-tenant and per-pool committed capacity (reserved slots, reservation-window metadata, recent commit events) and computes rolling statistics: EWMA of committed tokens (configurable half-life), windowed percentile sketches (P50/P95) and a decayed headroom estimate. Outputs are exposed as metrics: redwood.commitment.window_ewma, redwood.commitment.p95, redwood.commitment.headroom_estimate and an on-disk snapshot for operator diagnostics. Aggregator is implemented as an in-process agent within the dedicated-controller with a lightweight persistence layer to avoid traffic loss during short controller restarts. - Latency-Targeted Autoscaler: consumes aggregated commitment telemetry + online latency curves (occupancy -> latency percentiles) to synthesize predictive scale decisions. The autoscaler runs a short-horizon Monte Carlo forecast (default 30s lookahead) using sampled arrival rates and the commitment window to produce a suggested delta of GPU slots. Key safety knobs: damping_factor (0..1) to avoid oscillation, proactive_warmup_budget capped per-tenant, and a cooldown window after every scale event. It prefers warm-pool borrow when available and falls back to ephemeral provisioning. Implementation notes and rollout plan: - New feature gate: PredictiveLatencyAutoscale (off by default). - Configurable defaults are added to helm values under dedicated.autoscaler.predictive.* - Canary rollout: 10% of pools by label (team=canary) for 48h, track p99 latency, scale churn, and cost delta. - Observability: dashboards added (observability/dashboards/commitment-oversight.json) and new traces for predictive decisions. - Backwards compatibility: aggregator exposes telemetry but leaves existing reactive autoscaler unchanged until gate enabled. Checklist: - [x] commit aggregator implementation + unit tests - [x] predictive autoscaler core + unit tests - [x] e2e scenario harness (simulated traffic spikes) - [x] helm values & config docs - [x] operator snapshot persistence for aggregator - [x] observability dashboards and alert suggestions - [x] rollout playbook in docs/ops/proactive-scaling.md Commits: ["feat(telemetry): add commitment telemetry aggregator with EWMA windowing", "feat(autoscaler): latency-targeted predictive autoscale core loop and damping", "chore(helm): add predictive autoscaler defaults and feature-gate", "test(autoscaler): unit tests for forecasting and cooldown behavior", "docs(ops): proactive scaling runbook and dashboard links"] Files changed (high level): ["pkg/telemetry/commitment_aggregator.go", "pkg/telemetry/commitment_aggregator_test.go", "pkg/autoscaler/predictive_autoscaler.go", "pkg/autoscaler/predictive_model.go", "pkg/autoscaler/predictive_autoscaler_test.go", "operator/persistence/snapshots.go", "charts/dedicated/values.yaml", "observability/dashboards/commitment-oversight.json", "docs/ops/proactive-scaling.md", "integration/tests/e2e/predictive_scaling_scenarios.go", "scripts/bench/predictive_model_bench.go", "Makefile: add predictive test target"] Review conversation and notable threads: ["Diego: 'Nice end-to-end. Two concerns: 1) oscillation risk during correlated burst traffic, 2) accounting correctness when tenants have overlapping reservations.'", "Author (Maya): 'Added a damping_factor to the decision path and a 60s cooldown by default. For overlapping reservations we collapse by tenant id and compute committed tokens deduplicated by reservation hash; see commitment_aggregator.go line 148.'", "Priya: 'How do we ensure we don't starve the shared warm pool for small tenants?']", "Author: 'We introduced proactive_warmup_budget that is a per-tenant soft floor; the allocator pays from warm pool only if budget remains. Also added a fallback to ephemeral provisioning if warm pool < X percent'", "Liam: 'Please add a pressure test for long tail failure modes (controller flapping).', "Author: 'Added integration scenario with controller flapping and asserted no more than 1 scale-op per 2m in steady state. See integration/tests/e2e/predictive_scaling_scenarios.go'", "Diego (approved): 'Approach looks sound, leave in canary for 48h then promote if metrics stable.'", "SRE bot: 'CI flaky test recorded. Re-run requested.'", "CI (rerun): 'All checks passed after re-run.'"] CI checks and timeline: ["Initial CI (linux/unit): fail - TestPredictiveForecastRace (flake in stats aggregator)", "Triggered rerun after small locking fix in snapshots.go", "Rerun CI: pass", "Integration bench: pass (predictive_model_bench within cost budget)", "E2E (simulated): pass - no controller flapping detected under test harness"] Merge outcome: "merged via squash and merge. Rollout plan appended to docs and release notes. Canary label applied to 10% pools; operators notified in #dedicated-ops." Release notes: "Added Commitment Telemetry Aggregator and an opt-in Latency-Targeted Autoscaler (feature-gated). Provides rolling commitment metrics and a predictive scaling path to keep p99 latency within configured targets. Disabled by default; see docs/ops/proactive-scaling.md for rollout guidance." Notes for operators: "Observe metrics prefixed with redwood.commitment.* and redwood.autoscaler.predictive.*. If canary shows increased scale churn, reduce damping_factor to 0.7 or increase cooldown to 120s. Emergency rollback: flip PredictiveLatencyAutoscale feature gate off and drain predictive decisions via the operator-ctl command 'redwood operator predictive disable' (added in this PR)."

Maya: 'Added a damping_factor to the decision path and a 60s cooldown by default. For overlapping reservations we collapse by tenant id and compute committed tokens deduplicated by reservation hash; see commitment_aggregator.go line 148.'
Priya: 'How do we ensure we don't starve the shared warm pool for small tenants?'

Maya: 'We introduced proactive_warmup_budget that is a per-tenant soft floor; the allocator pays from warm pool only if budget remains. Also added a fallback to ephemeral provisioning if warm pool < X percent'
Liam: 'Please add a pressure test for long tail failure modes (controller flapping).'
Maya: 'Added integration scenario with controller flapping and asserted no more than 1 scale-op per 2m in steady state.'
Diego (approved): 'Approach looks sound, leave in canary for 48h then promote if metrics stable.'
release_notes: Added Commitment Telemetry Aggregator and opt-in Latency-Targeted Autoscaler (feature-gated). Exposes per-tenant rolling commitment metrics and predictive scaling to protect p99 latency SLOs. Default off; canary recommended.
notes_for_operators: Observe redwood.commitment.* and redwood.autoscaler.predictive.* metrics. Canary: label pools with team=canary. If churn increases reduce predictive.autoscaler.damping_factor or increase cooldown. Emergency rollback: disable PredictiveLatencyAutoscale feature gate.
